The Risk Disclosure Operator \mathcal{R}(\cdot) is a structured uncertainty estimator that maps historical outcome data \mathcal{D}_{\text{past}} to a bounded risk interval [\underline{r}, \overline{r}]. It operates under the assumption of exchangeability and stationarity of outcomes, enabling conformal prediction techniques. The operator's dual nature manifests in its ability to either provide a full predictive set or a scalar proxy depending on variant. Failure modes include overconfidence when \mathcal{D}_{\text{past}} is small or non-representative, and underfitting when \mathcal{R} is too coarse. The card variant enhances \mathcal{R} by incorporating past performance \mathcal{D}_{\text{perf}}, while the compact variant reduces dimensionality for efficiency. These variants form a family of risk estimators \mathcal{R}_{\theta}(\cdot) parameterized by \theta \in \{\text{card}, \text{compact}\}. The operator's epistemic robustness depends on \mathcal{D}_{\text{past}}'s representativeness and temporal consistency.
